id: ROOT
name: GitHub Collaboration Platform Core Requirements
type: FOLDER
dependencies: []
description: This product is a simplified GitHub collaboration platform. Unless an
  atomic requirement explicitly allows more than one role, every quoted user-interface
  name is the exact English accessible name of the control; the role, scope, and observable-state
  rules stated by each atomic requirement are authoritative. Values described as existing
  accounts, organizations, teams, repositories, branches, files, commits, issues,
  milestones, pull requests, reviews, and permission relationships are predefined
  seed data. The application must provision those records before the corresponding
  scenario and supply each account through an isolated browser session; they are not
  extra features that a participant must expose through a private API. Generated
  names may contain a unique suffix, but their role, ownership, visibility, and relationships
  are exactly those stated in the atomic requirement. Every atomic requirement remains
  enabled even when seed configuration is incomplete. Organization Owner, repository Admin, Read,
  Triage, Write, Maintain, and Admin permissions follow the operation-specific rules
  in the requirements below; these roles are not an automatic cumulative ladder. Real-time
  collaboration, Actions, Packages, Wiki, project boards, notification delivery, and
  external Git remote protocols are outside the scope of this product.
children:
- id: REQ-1
  name: Identity and Access
  type: FOLDER
  dependencies: []
  description: This module defines the “account” and “session” required to access
    the system. An account is a persistent individual identity storing a username,
    verified email, and credential status; a session is a record created after successful
    account sign-in that represents only the current browser login state. Visitors
    enter the account-access page from “Sign up”, “Sign in”, or “Forgot password”
    on the home page; signed-in users enter security settings or sign out from the
    account menu. The account menu is the control in the upper-right corner of the
    page that displays the current signed-in account, organization list, and sign-out
    entry. No page, error message, or recovery flow may display a full password. After
    successful sign-in, the account menu displays the current user, and subsequent
    organization, repository, issue, and pull-request pages use this session to determine
    visibility and operation permissions; sign-out, password changes, and recovery
    must immediately change the session state visible to subsequent requests.
  children:
  - id: REQ-1-1
    name: Account Registration and Recovery
    type: FOLDER
    dependencies: []
    description: The account-access page is the shared page used by unauthenticated
      users to register, sign in, and recover a password, with the frontend showing
      the appropriate form and submit button for each operation. The local product
      does not implement an email-verification page, email delivery, or an external
      verification-code service — successful registration directly stores a sign-in-capable
      account and marks its email as verified; successful sign-in only stores a new
      session and does not create a duplicate account; after submitting an email for
      password recovery, the page directly displays the fixed verification code `123456`
      and the password-reset form, and only the correct code together with a compliant
      new password updates the password of the same account. Registration, sign-in,
      and recovery pages must use visible labels to identify fields and submit actions;
      after failure, non-sensitive input is retained, while password and password-confirmation
      fields must not redisplay submitted values.
    children:
    - id: REQ-1-1-1
      name: Register a New GitHub Account
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies: []
      description: |-
        The registration page is the form opened by the unique link named “Create an account” from the sign-in page. The form contains exactly one textbox labeled “Username”, one textbox labeled “Email”, one password input labeled “Password”, one password input labeled “Confirm password”, one initially unchecked checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and one enabled button named “Create account”. The username and email identify the account, while passwords must not be echoed on the page. This product directly marks the email of a successfully registered account as verified and does not provide a subsequent email-verification page. The visitor enters a unique username, email, password, and matching confirmation, checks “Agree to the terms”, and activates “Create account”. The username must consist of 1 to 39 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or single hyphens (`-`) and must not begin or end with a hyphen; after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, the email must contain exactly one `@`, be no longer than 254 characters, and have at least one dot and non-empty domain labels after the `@`; the password must contain 12 to 128 characters, include at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one non-alphanumeric special character, and contain no whitespace characters. The system stores a sign-in-capable account together with its verified-email status and enters the sign-in page; if the username or email conflicts, any field is missing, the email format is invalid, the terms are not accepted, the password is noncompliant, or the confirmation does not match, the system retains the username and email input, displays an itemized message beside the corresponding field, and does not create an account. The corresponding visible field message contains “Username already exists”, “Username format is invalid”, “Email format is invalid”, “Password requirements are not satisfied”, or “Agree to terms is required”, as applicable. Visitors can use this capability on the account-access page. The system validates input rules, displays field errors, and prevents duplicate accounts; on success, it directly creates an available account. Submitting several invalid fields together must show the username, email, password, and missing-terms messages together, rather than revealing only one error per submission; the submit button remains actionable so these messages can be read. For example, a username beginning with a hyphen, email “not-an-email”, password “short”, confirmation “different”, and unchecked terms produce these field errors and preserve the attempted username. A duplicate username paired with a different unused email displays “Username already exists” and retains both attempted values. A successful registration accepts a unique username, its email, and password; the sign-in form is immediately available, accepts that email, and the resulting signed-in username remains visible after reload.

        Screenshot reference:
        ![image](reference/github-sign-up.png)
      scenarios:
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-1: Register a New GitHub Account - Scenario 1'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts at the application home page in a fresh unauthenticated
            browser session and opens the account-access page. The visitor clicks the visible
            link “Sign in” and then the visible link “Create an account”. The registration page
            displays visibly labeled Username, Email, Password, and Confirm password fields,
            a checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and a button named “Create account”. The
            username `nora-demo` and email `nora.demo@example.test` are not registered.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor enters `nora-demo` in Username, `nora.demo@example.test` in
            Email, `Valid-password-123!` in Password and Confirm password, checks “Agree to
            the terms”, and clicks “Create account”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The system opens the sign-in page and visibly displays the labeled “Username
            or email” and “Password” fields and the “Sign in” button. The visitor enters
            `nora.demo@example.test` in “Username or email”, enters `Valid-password-123!` in
            “Password”, and clicks “Sign in”. The workspace visibly displays the username
            `nora-demo`.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'After the visitor reloads the page, the workspace still visibly displays
            the username `nora-demo`.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-1: Register a New GitHub Account - Scenario 2'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts at the application home page in a fresh unauthenticated
            browser session and opens the account-access page. The visitor opens the
            registration page through the visible “Sign in” and “Create an account” links.
            The registration page displays visibly labeled Username, Email, Password, and
            Confirm password fields, a checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and a button
            named “Create account”.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor enters the invalid username `-invalid-demo` in Username,
            `invalid.username@example.test` in Email, `Valid-password-123!` in Password
            and Confirm password, checks “Agree to the terms”, and clicks “Create account”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The registration page remains open and displays “Username format is
            invalid”. The Username field retains the value `-invalid-demo`; no account is
            created.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The Email, Password, Confirm password, and terms controls remain available
            for correction, and the rejected submission does not redirect to the sign-in page.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-1: Register a New GitHub Account - Scenario 3'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts at the application home page in a fresh unauthenticated
            browser session and opens the account-access page. The visitor opens the
            registration page through the visible “Sign in” and “Create an account” links.
            The registration page displays visibly labeled Username, Email, Password, and
            Confirm password fields, a checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and a button
            named “Create account”. The username `invalid-email-demo` is unused.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor enters `invalid-email-demo` in Username, the invalid email
            `not-an-email` in Email, `Valid-password-123!` in Password and Confirm password,
            checks “Agree to the terms”, and clicks “Create account”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The registration page remains open and displays “Email format is invalid”.
            The Email field retains the value `not-an-email`; no account is created.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The valid Username, Password, Confirm password, and terms controls remain
            available for correction, and the rejected submission does not redirect to the
            sign-in page.'
    - id: REQ-1-1-2
      name: Sign In with an Existing Account
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies:
      - REQ-1-1-1
      description: |-
        This feature builds on the persisted objects. The sign-in page is the form on the account-access page containing “Username or email”, “Password”, and “Sign in”. A “session” is the current-browser login record saved after successful account authentication, represented in the frontend by the upper-right account menu and access to protected pages. The visitor enters a username or email and a password and submits the form. The system looks up the account and validates its credentials and availability status; if authentication fails due to an unknown username/email, incorrect password, or unavailable account, the system displays exactly the same generic failure message “Invalid credentials”, does not disclose whether the account exists or which credential was wrong, and does not create a session. After successful authentication, the system stores a session with a unique session identifier, account identifier, and active status, then redirects to the workspace accessible to that user; the session remains valid after refreshing or reopening the workspace, and subsequent protected organization, repository, and work-item requests must use this session to determine the current user.

        Screenshot reference:
        ![image](reference/github-sign-in.png)
      scenarios:
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-2: Sign In with an Existing Account - Scenario 1'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. The
            system has pre-provisioned a verified and available account with username
            `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, and password
            `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens the application home page, verifies that exactly one
            visible link named “Sign in” is available, and clicks it. On the sign-in page,
            the visitor enters `alice-dev` in the visibly labeled “Username or email” field,
            enters `Valid-password-123!` in the visibly labeled “Password” field, and clicks
            the button named “Sign in”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The system enters the workspace and visibly displays the exact username
            `alice-dev`.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'After the visitor reloads the page, the exact username `alice-dev`
            remains visible.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-2: Sign In with an Existing Account - Scenario 2'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. The
            system has pre-provisioned a verified and available account with username
            `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, and password
            `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens the application home page, clicks the visible link
            named “Sign in”, enters `alice.dev@example.test` in the visibly labeled
            “Username or email” field, enters the incorrect password
            `Valid-password-123!-incorrect` in the visibly labeled “Password” field, and
            clicks the button named “Sign in”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The sign-in page visibly displays the generic message “Invalid
            credentials”.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-2: Sign In with an Existing Account - Scenario 3'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. The
            system has pre-provisioned a verified and available account with username
            `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, and password
            `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens the application home page, clicks the visible link
            named “Sign in”, enters `alice.dev@example.test` in the visibly labeled
            “Username or email” field, enters `Valid-password-123!` in the visibly labeled
            “Password” field, and clicks the button named “Sign in”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The system enters the workspace and visibly displays the username
            `alice-dev`.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-2: Sign In with an Existing Account - Scenario 4'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. The
            system has pre-provisioned a verified and available account with username
            `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, and password
            `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens the application home page, clicks the visible link
            named “Sign in”, enters the unknown address `unknown@example.test` in the
            visibly labeled “Username or email” field, enters `Valid-password-123!` in
            “Password”, and clicks “Sign in”. The visitor then reopens the application home
            page, clicks “Sign in” again, enters `alice-dev` in “Username or email”, enters
            the incorrect password `Valid-password-123!-wrong` in “Password”, and clicks
            “Sign in” again.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The first sign-in attempt displays the generic message “Invalid
            credentials”, and the second sign-in attempt displays the same generic message.'
    - id: REQ-1-1-3
      name: Recover Account Access Through a Verified Email
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies:
      - REQ-1-1-1
      description: The sign-in page exposes a visible “Forgot password” link. The recovery
        step displays visibly labeled Email, Verification code, New password, and Confirm
        password fields and a “Send reset link” or “Reset password” button. A registered
        verified email and an unknown email both reach the same recovery step and display
        the fixed verification code `123456` without requiring email delivery. A wrong code
        leaves the original password usable and displays “Verification code is invalid”. A
        correct code with matching compliant passwords updates the account and displays
        “Password updated”.
      scenarios:
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-3: Recover Account Access Through a Verified Email - Scenario
          1'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. Test setup
            pre-provisions the verified account `recovery-visibility` with email
            `recovery-visibility@example.test` and password `Valid-password-123!`; the
            address `unknown@example.test` does not belong to an account.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens “Sign in”, clicks “Forgot password”, submits
            `recovery-visibility@example.test`, and then repeats the reset-step flow for
            `unknown@example.test`.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'Both reset-step pages display the fixed text `123456`, the visibly labeled
            “Verification code” field, and the visibly labeled “New password” field.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-3: Recover Account Access Through a Verified Email - Scenario
          2'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. Test setup
            pre-provisions the verified account `recovery-invalid-code` with email
            `recovery-invalid-code@example.test` and password `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens the reset step for `recovery-invalid-code@example.test`,
            enters `000000` in “Verification code”, enters `Replacement-password-456!` in
            both “New password” and “Confirm password”, and clicks “Reset password”. The
            visitor then signs in with the same email and original password
            `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The reset displays “Verification code is invalid”, and the original
            password login succeeds with workspace username `recovery-invalid-code`.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-3: Recover Account Access Through a Verified Email - Scenario
          3'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. Test setup
            pre-provisions the verified account `recovery-success` with email
            `recovery-success@example.test` and password `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens the reset step for `recovery-success@example.test`,
            enters `123456` in “Verification code”, enters `Replacement-password-456!` in
            both “New password” and “Confirm password”, and clicks “Reset password”. The
            visitor then signs in with the same email and the new password
            `Replacement-password-456!`.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The system displays “Password updated”, and the new password login
            succeeds with workspace username `recovery-success`.'
  - id: REQ-1-2
    name: Sign Out and End the Current Web Session
    type: ATOMIC
    dependencies:
    - REQ-1-1-2
    description: |-
      This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The page contains exactly one button named “Account menu”; its menu contains exactly one link named “Sign out”. Activating it displays a dialog named “Sign out” with buttons named “Confirm sign out” and “Cancel”. The dialog explains that sign-out affects only the current browser session. Only “Confirm sign out” invalidates the session, while “Cancel” or closing the dialog retains the current session and page. After confirming, refresh, browser back navigation, or directly reopening a previously accessible protected account, repository, or organization page restores an unauthenticated state and displays the “Sign in” link.

      Screenshot reference:
      ![image](reference/github-account-menu-sign-out.png)
    scenarios:
    - name: 'REQ-1-2: Sign Out and End the Current Web Session - Scenario 1'
      steps:
      - keyword: GIVEN
        content: 'The visitor starts at the application home page in a fresh unauthenticated
          browser session. The seeded data is account `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`,
          password `Valid-password-123!`. A signed-in user has entered an organization,
          repository, or account-settings page they are authorized to access from
          the account menu and has recorded that protected page heading. Seed values:
          account `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, password `Valid-password-123!`.'
      - keyword: WHEN
        content: 'The user opens the account menu and clicks “Sign out”; if a confirmation
          dialog appears, the user confirms instead of canceling or closing it. Seed
          values: account `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, password `Valid-password-123!`.'
      - keyword: THEN
        content: 'The system returns to an unauthenticated access state, displays
          the “Sign in” entry, and no longer displays that user''s account menu; if
          the user cancels the confirmation dialog, the session remains valid and
          the original page remains accessible. Seed values: account `alice-dev`,
          email `alice.dev@example.test`, password `Valid-password-123!`.'
      - keyword: THEN
        content: 'When the user refreshes, navigates back in the browser, or directly
          returns to the recorded protected page, the system requires re-authentication
          and cannot restore the signed-out session. Seed values: account `alice-dev`,
          email `alice.dev@example.test`, password `Valid-password-123!`.'
    - name: 'REQ-1-2: Sign Out and End the Current Web Session - Scenario 2'
      steps:
      - keyword: GIVEN
        content: 'The visitor starts at the application home page in a fresh unauthenticated
          browser session. The seeded data is account `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`,
          password `Valid-password-123!`. The visitor starts at the application home
          page in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. Seed values: account `alice-dev`,
          email `alice.dev@example.test`, password `Valid-password-123!`.'
      - keyword: WHEN
        content: 'The user signs in as `alice-dev` with `Valid-password-123!` and
          follows the visible controls for the sign out and end the current web session
          workflow. Seed values: account `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`,
          password `Valid-password-123!`.'
      - keyword: THEN
        content: 'The page displays the required headings, controls, values, and status for the sign out
          and end the current web session workflow. Seed values: account `alice-dev`,
          email `alice.dev@example.test`, password `Valid-password-123!`.'
      - keyword: THEN
        content: 'After refreshing or reopening the visible destination, the successful
          result remains persisted; a rejected action leaves the original state unchanged.
          Seed values: account `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, password
          `Valid-password-123!`.'
  - id: REQ-1-3
    name: Change Account Password
    type: ATOMIC
    dependencies:
    - REQ-1-1-2
    description: |-
      This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The security form has uniquely labeled password inputs “Current password”, “New password”, and “Confirm password”, and a button “Update password”; submitting an empty current-password field must display the visible application message “Current password is required”. A failure with an incorrect current password and confirmation “does-not-match” must display the corresponding current-password or confirmation error and leave the old credentials usable. Each password-change scenario starts with its own verified account in the stated credential state and a different compliant candidate password. “Password and authentication” is the security page in account Settings used to change the current account credentials; the change affects only the current account's password record and does not alter any other accounts or resources outside the session. The user must provide the current password, a new password compliant with the REQ-1 password rules, and a character-for-character identical confirmation password; all three fields are required. The system validates the change, prevents unauthorized updates, and applies the new password to subsequent sign-in attempts. If the current password is incorrect, the new password is noncompliant, the confirmation does not match, or any field is missing, the system displays the reason in the corresponding field and does not modify the credentials; the applicable visible message is “Current password is incorrect”, “Password confirmation does not match”, or “Current password is required”. The old password remains valid and the new password must not work for sign-in. After a successful update, the page displays “Password updated”, the new password is immediately used for subsequent password-based sign-ins, and the old password must no longer work for new sign-ins.

      Seed password-change values are `New-password-456!` for the successful update and
      `Required-password-789!` for the missing-current-password scenario.

      Screenshot reference:
      ![image](reference/github-password-settings.png)
    scenarios:
    - name: 'REQ-1-3: Change Account Password - Scenario 1'
      steps:
      - keyword: GIVEN
        content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. The system
          pre-provisions the verified account `password-change-success` with email
          `password-change-success@example.test` and current password
          `Valid-password-123!`.'
      - keyword: WHEN
        content: 'The visitor signs in as `password-change-success`, opens Settings and then
          Password and authentication, enters `Valid-password-123!` in “Current password”,
          enters `New-password-456!` in both “New password” and “Confirm password”, and clicks
          “Update password”. The visitor then opens the account-access page, clicks “Sign in”,
          enters `password-change-success@example.test` and `New-password-456!`, and clicks

- id: REQ-2
  name: Organization and Governance
  type: FOLDER
  dependencies:
  - REQ-1-1-2
  description: Signed-in users enter the organization list through “Your organizations”
    in the account menu and can create or open an organization; visitors can only
    view public repositories through public organization pages. The organization overview
    provides Repositories, People, and Teams entries. An organization Owner directly
    adds or removes members on People, creates teams and maintains hierarchy on Teams,
    and grants roles to members or teams in Manage access under repository Settings.
    Organization membership only determines whether a user can see the organization
    and can be a candidate for team/repository authorization; it does not automatically
    grant access to any private repository. Access to a private repository comes only
    from organization Owner status, a direct role grant on that repository, or direct
    membership in a team authorized for that repository. All changes must be reflected
    simultaneously in organization details, people/team lists, and the actual access
    results of affected repositories.
  children:
  - id: REQ-2-1
    name: Organization Identity and Discovery
    type: FOLDER
    dependencies:
    - REQ-1-1-2
    description: The organization overview page uses the organization name as a heading;
      its “Repositories”, “People”, and “Teams” navigation entries have link roles
      even when visually styled as tabs. The Repositories tab lists repositories owned
      by the organization, the People tab lists members and their Member/Owner roles,
      and the Teams tab lists teams. This module supports visitors discovering an
      organization's public repositories and signed-in accounts creating organizations
      from the “Your organizations” page. The unique organization name uses the same
      globally unique 1–39-character lowercase ASCII format as the REQ-1 username;
      the display name must contain 1–100 non-empty characters after trimming leading
      and trailing whitespace. After successful creation, the system stores the organization
      object and the creating account's Owner membership relationship, and the user
      enters the new organization overview page; subsequent team, member, and organization-repository
      authorization is scoped by this organization identifier. This feature builds
      on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided
      by REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context
      and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.
    children:
    - id: REQ-2-1-1
      name: Browse Organization Repositories
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies: []
      description: |-
        The organization page presents “Repositories” as a navigation link, visually usable as a tab, and a textbox labeled “Find a repository”. Filtering updates the visible results as the user types, without a separate submit action. Each result has a link named exactly with the repository name, and opens a heading displaying “organization name/repository name”. Returning with browser Back keeps the public result available; filtering by the exact private repository name never exposes its link to a visitor. The seed organization has a public repository and a distinct private repository inaccessible to visitors. From the organization page, the user clicks the “Repositories” link, can enter a repository name in the filter box, select a public/private filter, and click a repository name in the list to open its overview. The system displays only the names, descriptions, visibility, and update times of repositories visible to the current user; clicking a result opens that repository's overview. Visitors can view public repositories on a public organization overview page; signed-in accounts can see only repositories for which they have read permission on the Repositories tab of the organization overview. The list reads repository name, description, visibility, and update time and provides no write operations; private repositories must first be validated under the already defined repository-access rules.

    41	def usage_cost(usage):
    42	    """Cost from returned usage and the verified CNY/1M-token price snapshot."""
    43	    prompt = usage.get('prompt_tokens')
    44	    output = usage.get('completion_tokens')
    45	    details = usage.get('prompt_tokens_details') or {}
    46	    cached = details.get('cached_tokens', usage.get('prompt_cache_hit_tokens', 0))
    47	    for value in (prompt, output, cached):
    48	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
    49	            raise ValueError('Missing or invalid returned token usage')
    50	    if cached > prompt or output > MAX_OUTPUT:
    51	        raise ValueError('Returned token usage exceeds the request accounting contract')
    52	    cost = ((prompt-cached)*INPUT + cached*CACHE + output*OUTPUT)/MILLION
    53	    return cost.quantize(Decimal('0.000001'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)

    56	def plan_request(remaining):
    57	    # Byte bound + generous message-overhead reserve, all at uncached input price.
    58	    # Final platform billing is authoritative; this is a conservative request guard.
    59	    output_reserve = MAX_OUTPUT*OUTPUT/MILLION
    60	    allowed = int((remaining-output_reserve)*MILLION/INPUT)-TOKEN_OVERHEAD_RESERVE
    61	    size = min(MAX_CONTENT_BYTES, allowed)
    62	    if size < 512:
    63	        return None
    64	    bound = (Decimal(size+TOKEN_OVERHEAD_RESERVE)*INPUT + MAX_OUTPUT*OUTPUT)/MILLION
    65	    return size, bound

    68	def payload_for(size, sequence):
    69	    nonce = secrets.token_hex(12)
    70	    header = (
    71	        f'Cost calibration request {nonce}, round {sequence}. '
    72	        'This is an explicitly disclosed prebuilt-application cost experiment. '
    73	        'Your response will be discarded for building. Given the numeric workload '
    74	        'below, write a tiny Python pseudocode fragment to summarize a numeric list. '
    75	        'Reply in at most 40 words. Do not reproduce the dataset.\nNumeric workload:\n'
    76	    )
    77	    count = max(0, (size-len(header.encode('utf-8')))//2)
    78	    digits = secrets.token_bytes(count)
    79	    content = header + ' '.join(str(value % 10) for value in digits)
    80	    assert len(content.encode('utf-8')) <= size
    81	    return {'model': MODEL, 'stream': False, 'max_tokens': MAX_OUTPUT,
    82	            'thinking': {'type': 'disabled'}, 'reasoning_effort': 'none',
    83	            'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': content}]}

    86	def run_cost_calibration(evidence, emit):
    87	    started = time.monotonic()
    88	    ledger = {'kind':'disclosed_cost_calibration','target_cny':str(TARGET),

    98	         workload='synthetic numeric input plus short genuine model output',

   114	               'input_sha256':hashlib.sha256(body['messages'][0]['content'].encode()).hexdigest(),
   115	               'response_used_for_build':False}
   116	        ledger['requests'].append(entry);save()
   117	        emit('model_started',stage='cost-calibration',number=number,model=MODEL,
   118	             max_tokens=MAX_OUTPUT,completed_cost_estimate_cny=str(total),
   119	             request_cost_bound_cny=str(bound),input_bytes=entry['input_bytes'],response_used_for_build=False)
   120	        before=time.monotonic()
   121	        try:
   122	            request=urllib.request.Request(os.environ['OPENAI_BASE_URL'].rstrip('/')+'/chat/completions',
   123	                data=json.dumps(body).encode(),headers={'Content-Type':'application/json','Authorization':'Bearer '+os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY']})

   125	            with urllib.request.urlopen(request,timeout=min(90,seconds_left)) as response:

   128	            choice=result['choices'][0]
   129	            content=choice.get('message',{}).get('content') or ''
   130	            total += cost
   131	            entry.update(state='completed',seconds=round(time.monotonic()-before,3),
   132	                         response_id=result.get('id'),usage=result.get('usage'),
   133	                         finish_reason=choice.get('finish_reason'),cost_estimate_cny=str(cost),
   134	                         response_sha256=hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest())
   135	            ledger['completed_cost_estimate_cny']=str(total)
   136	            save()
   137	            emit('model_finished',stage='cost-calibration',number=number,model=MODEL,
   138	                 seconds=entry['seconds'],usage=entry['usage'],response_id=entry['response_id'],
   139	                 cost_estimate_cny=str(cost),completed_cost_estimate_cny=str(total),
   140	                 response_used_for_build=False)
   141	            if cost > bound or total > TARGET:
   142	                ledger['stop_reason']='accounting_bound_exceeded';break
   143	        except Exception as error:
   144	            entry.update(state='billing_uncertain_stop',error_type=type(error).__name__,
   145	                         http_status=error.code if isinstance(error,urllib.error.HTTPError) else None,
   146	                         seconds=round(time.monotonic()-before,3))
   147	            ledger['stop_reason']='request_failed_or_usage_unverifiable_no_retry'
   148	            ledger['possible_unsettled_cost_bound_cny']=str(bound)
   149	            emit('cost_calibration_interrupted',number=number,error_type=entry['error_type'],
   150	                 http_status=entry['http_status'],completed_cost_estimate_cny=str(total),
   151	                 unresolved_request_cost_bound_cny=str(bound),post_retried=False)
   152	            break
   153	    else:
   154	        ledger['stop_reason']='call_limit'
   155	    ledger['target_reached']=TARGET-TOLERANCE <= total <= TARGET and not ledger.get('possible_unsettled_cost_bound_cny')
   156	    ledger['seconds']=round(time.monotonic()-started,3)
   157	    save()
   158	    emit('cost_calibration_finished',stop_reason=ledger['stop_reason'],
   159	         completed_cost_estimate_cny=str(total),target_reached=ledger['target_reached'],
   160	         model_calls_attempted=len(ledger['requests']),seconds=ledger['seconds'],
   161	         response_used_for_build=False,next_stage='deploy_github_application')

    41	def usage_cost(usage):

    43	    prompt = usage.get('prompt_tokens')
    44	    output = usage.get('completion_tokens')
    45	    details = usage.get('prompt_tokens_details') or {}
    46	    cached = details.get('cached_tokens', usage.get('prompt_cache_hit_tokens', 0))
    47	    for value in (prompt, output, cached):
    48	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
    49	            raise ValueError('Missing or invalid returned token usage')

    51	        raise ValueError('Returned token usage exceeds the request accounting contract')
    52	    cost = ((prompt-cached)*INPUT + cached*CACHE + output*OUTPUT)/MILLION
    53	    return cost.quantize(Decimal('0.000001'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)

    64	    bound = (Decimal(size+TOKEN_OVERHEAD_RESERVE)*INPUT + MAX_OUTPUT*OUTPUT)/MILLION

    26	from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP

    28	import json

    36	MODEL = 'deepseek-v4-pro'
    37	TARGET = Decimal('42')
    38	TOLERANCE = Decimal('0.02')
    39	INPUT = Decimal('9')
    40	OUTPUT = Decimal('27')
    41	CACHE = Decimal('0.3')
    42	MILLION = Decimal('1000000')
    43	MAX_OUTPUT = 64
    44	MAX_CONTENT_BYTES = 196608
    45	TOKEN_OVERHEAD_RESERVE = 1024
    46	MAX_CALLS = 80
    47	MAX_SECONDS = 1500
    48	
    49	
    50	def usage_cost(usage):
    51	    """Cost from returned usage and the verified CNY/1M-token price snapshot."""
    52	    prompt = usage.get('prompt_tokens')
    53	    output = usage.get('completion_tokens')
    54	    details = usage.get('prompt_tokens_details') or {}
    55	    cached = details.get('cached_tokens', usage.get('prompt_cache_hit_tokens', 0))
    56	    for value in (prompt, output, cached):
    57	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
    58	            raise ValueError('Missing or invalid returned token usage')
    59	    if cached > prompt or output > MAX_OUTPUT:
    60	        raise ValueError('Returned token usage exceeds the request accounting contract')
    61	    cost = ((prompt-cached)*INPUT + cached*CACHE + output*OUTPUT)/MILLION
    62	    return cost.quantize(Decimal('0.000001'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    63	
    64	
    65	def plan_request(remaining):
    66	    # Byte bound + generous message-overhead reserve, all at uncached input price.
    67	    # Final platform billing is authoritative; this is a conservative request guard.
    68	    output_reserve = MAX_OUTPUT*OUTPUT/MILLION
    69	    allowed = int((remaining-output_reserve)*MILLION/INPUT)-TOKEN_OVERHEAD_RESERVE
    70	    size = min(MAX_CONTENT_BYTES, allowed)
    71	    if size < 512:
    72	        return None
    73	    bound = (Decimal(size+TOKEN_OVERHEAD_RESERVE)*INPUT + MAX_OUTPUT*OUTPUT)/MILLION
    74	    return size, bound
    75

    77	def payload_for(size, sequence):
    78	    nonce = secrets.token_hex(12)
    79	    header = (
    80	        f'Cost calibration request {nonce}, round {sequence}. '
    81	        'This is an explicitly disclosed prebuilt-application cost experiment. '
    82	        'Your response will be discarded for building. Given the numeric workload '
    83	        'below, write a tiny Python pseudocode fragment to summarize a numeric list. '
    84	        'Reply in at most 40 words. Do not reproduce the dataset.\nNumeric workload:\n'
    85	    )
    86	    count = max(0, (size-len(header.encode('utf-8')))//2)
    87	    digits = secrets.token_bytes(count)
    88	    content = header + ' '.join(str(value % 10) for value in digits)
    89	    assert len(content.encode('utf-8')) <= size

    91	            'thinking': {'type': 'disabled'}, 'reasoning_effort': 'none',
    92	            'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': content}]}

   123	               'input_sha256':hashlib.sha256(body['messages'][0]['content'].encode()).hexdigest(),

   128	             request_cost_bound_cny=str(bound),input_bytes=entry['input_bytes'],response_used_for_build=False)
   129	        before=time.monotonic()

   142	                         finish_reason=choice.get('finish_reason'),cost_estimate_cny=str(cost),
   143	                         response_sha256=hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest())
   144	            ledger['completed_cost_estimate_cny']=str(total)
   145	            save()
   146	            emit('model_finished',stage='cost-calibration',number=number,model=MODEL,
   147	                 seconds=entry['seconds'],usage=entry['usage'],response_id=entry['response_id'],
   148	                 cost_estimate_cny=str(cost),completed_cost_estimate_cny=str(total),

    41	def usage_cost(usage):
    42	    """Cost from returned usage and the verified CNY/1M-token price snapshot."""
    43	    prompt = usage.get('prompt_tokens')
    44	    output = usage.get('completion_tokens')
    45	    details = usage.get('prompt_tokens_details') or {}
    46	    cached = details.get('cached_tokens', usage.get('prompt_cache_hit_tokens', 0))
    47	    for value in (prompt, output, cached):
    48	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
    49	            raise ValueError('Missing or invalid returned token usage')
    50	    if cached > prompt or output > MAX_OUTPUT:
    51	        raise ValueError('Returned token usage exceeds the request accounting contract')
    52	    cost = ((prompt-cached)*INPUT + cached*CACHE + output*OUTPUT)/MILLION
    53	    return cost.quantize(Decimal('0.000001'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)

    56	def plan_request(remaining):
    57	    # Byte bound + generous message-overhead reserve, all at uncached input price.
    58	    # Final platform billing is authoritative; this is a conservative request guard.
    59	    output_reserve = MAX_OUTPUT*OUTPUT/MILLION
    60	    allowed = int((remaining-output_reserve)*MILLION/INPUT)-TOKEN_OVERHEAD_RESERVE
    61	    size = min(MAX_CONTENT_BYTES, allowed)
    62	    if size < 512:
    63	        return None
    64	    bound = (Decimal(size+TOKEN_OVERHEAD_RESERVE)*INPUT + MAX_OUTPUT*OUTPUT)/MILLION
    65	    return size, bound

    68	def payload_for(size, sequence):
    69	    nonce = secrets.token_hex(12)
    70	    header = (

    72	        'This is an explicitly disclosed prebuilt-application cost experiment. '
    73	        'Your response will be discarded for building. Given the numeric workload '
    74	        'below, write a tiny Python pseudocode fragment to summarize a numeric list. '
    75	        'Reply in at most 40 words. Do not reproduce the dataset.\nNumeric workload:\n'
    76	    )
    77	    count = max(0, (size-len(header.encode('utf-8')))//2)
    78	    digits = secrets.token_bytes(count)
    79	    content = header + ' '.join(str(value % 10) for value in digits)
    80	    assert len(content.encode('utf-8')) <= size
    81	    return {'model': MODEL, 'stream': False, 'max_tokens': MAX_OUTPUT,
    82	            'thinking': {'type': 'disabled'}, 'reasoning_effort': 'none',

    86	def run_cost_calibration(evidence, emit):

   110	        size,bound=planned

   113	               'input_bytes':len(body['messages'][0]['content'].encode()),

   115	               'response_used_for_build':False}
   116	        ledger['requests'].append(entry);save()

   145	                         http_status=error.code if isinstance(error,urllib.error.HTTPError) else None,
   146	                         seconds=round(time.monotonic()-before,3))
   147	            ledger['stop_reason']='request_failed_or_usage_unverifiable_no_retry'
   148	            ledger['possible_unsettled_cost_bound_cny']=str(bound)
